description: Intuit is a business software company serving roughly 100 million customers worldwide. It is the top provider of small business accounting and online tax preparation software in the U.S. thanks to flagship products QuickBooks and TurboTax, respectively. Other major offerings include personal finance and credit monitoring service Credit Karma and automated email marketing platform Mailchimp. Scott Cook and Tom Proulx founded the company in 1983.

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription: America’s income inequality and wealth gap might not be as wide if we didn’t also have a financial literacy gap: 88% of Americans say high school didn’t equip them to think about managing money. Intuit, the financial software company, has designed a high-school level curriculum—Intuit for Education—that focuses on debt and credit, taxes, budgeting, and investment principles. The program, which is free, has been adopted by more than 30,000 teachers and reached 4.6 million students nationwide; this year it’s expanding to colleges and universities. (What’s in it for Intuit: The students get introduced to its financial-management tools, including QuickBooks, TurboTax, and Credit Karma.)

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
Intuit has recognized that the financial services and technology industry needs to better serve those who have been historically underrepresented, and it’s doing its part through recruitment and retention: 34% of its global tech roles were held by women as of May 2023, and 16.3% of employees came from underrepresented racial backgrounds as of last July.
 

On the pay side, Intuit reports full compensation equity between men and women, as well as between white and underrepresented racial groups in the U.S.
 

Intuit has been closely involved in the construction of the Intuit Dome, the future Inglewood, Calif., home of the NBA’s Los Angeles Clippers. During construction, Intuit is investing in financial and entrepreneurial education programs for local school districts, which it will continue once the stadium is built. It is also hosting events such as free taxpayer assistance sessions and educational and networking workshops, geared toward underrepresented small-business leaders in the community.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription:
The financial software giant, whose products include TurboTax and QuickBooks, continues its more than two decades long tenure on the Best Companies to Work For list.

  • When Intuit reopened its offices in May 2022, it hosted a (Re)connect program with events and experiences to welcome staffers back.

  • To facilitate its new hybrid work model, Intuit offers managers more training, including a Leading Your Team Into Hybrid module.

  • Intuit increased its annual well-being benefit to $1,300, and employees can use it to cover a wide variety of expenses, from conventional gym memberships to financial planning services to day care and even electric vehicles.

  • “Everything at Intuit is about people, whether you are a worker or customer, it’s all about you. Intuit takes pride in listening and taking care of everyone,” says one employee. “It’s the backbone of our company, and it shows in our benefits, products, and values.”

rankings.title: Fortune 50 AI Innovators
rankings.itemDescription: When it comes to developing useful AI systems, data is everything. And financial software giant Intuit, maker of TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp, has a lot of it. Earlier this year, the company announced GenOS, its proprietary operating system for generative AI development that works with best-in-class third-party large language models (LLMs), as well as Intuit’s own custom-trained financial LLMs, fine-tuned to solve tax, accounting, cash flow, personal finance, and marketing challenges. The company works with over 24,000 financial institutions, and they generate 65 billion machine learning predictions per day. “We don’t have a group on the side working on AI. It is core to everything that we design,” Intuit CEO Sasan Goodarzi said at a Fortune conference last year. The company continues to incorporate AI into its human financial expert offerings in its TurboTax Live and QuickBooks Live products, and in September released Intuit Assist—the company’s generative-AI-powered financial assistant that works across all Intuit products.

rankings.title: Fortune Modern Board 25
rankings.itemDescription: The software company earned a spot on the Modern Board 25 for its notable expertise and diversity. Members of its 11-person board range in age from 46 to 70, and four are women. In May, it added LinkedIn CEO Ryan Roslansky and Zoom CEO Eric Yuan. The board includes other current and former chief executives, including Intuit cofounder and ex-CEO Scott Cook; Ancestry.com CEO Deborah Liu; Oportun CEO Raul Vazquez; Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana; as well as directors with ties to Hearst and Amazon. Intuit has avoided mass layoffs in 2023 as other tech firms shed staff. The company aims for revenue growth of approximately 10% to 12% this fiscal year and an operating income of at least $2.8 billion.

rankings.title: Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For
rankings.itemDescription: Intuit, the global financial platform behind TurboTax and QuickBooks, has kept its employees’ well-being a priority since the pandemic began. Last year, it expanded the $1,300 Well-Being for Life benefit—which reimburses any expense aligning with employees’ physical, emotional, or financial well-being—to include costs like nannies, tutors, and financial planning services. In its effort to “power prosperity,” Intuit’s Prosperity Hubs program, launched in 2016, has led to the creation of thousands of full-time and seasonal jobs across eight underserved communities in the U.S., Canada, and the U.K. “Executive leadership listens and acts to ensure employees are supported and successful,” notes one staffer. Indeed, in 2021, 1,000 jobs (28% of openings) were filled internally.
